notes: Single source of truth for every threshold, assumption and scenario in the consumption analytics pack. Changing a value here and re-running scripts/refresh_all.py changes every status flag, commentary line and what-if result. Values marked auto are derived from the data at refresh time.

thresholds.name: Data as at (report date)
thresholds.use: Later of last successful load and last closed period; shown on every page and stamped on every answer

thresholds.name: Consumption-to-investment ratio band
thresholds.use: Below 0.80 = over-purchasing; above 1.05 = drawing down opening stock

thresholds.name: Consumption variance vs budget - investigate above
thresholds.use: Beyond this band the variance requires written commentary and an owner

thresholds.name: Materiality for mandatory commentary
thresholds.use: PKR 250,000 or 10% of the category budget, whichever is lower

thresholds.name: Days of cover - critical threshold
thresholds.use: Raise a purchase requisition or transfer immediately

thresholds.name: Days of cover - watch threshold
thresholds.use: Include in the next monthly purchase plan

thresholds.name: Expiry alert window
thresholds.use: Redistribute, consume first, or write off before expiry

thresholds.name: Price variance - investigate above
thresholds.use: Compare supplier quotes and check contract validity

thresholds.name: Unattributed consumption ceiling
thresholds.use: Above this, escalate to the project-coding owner

thresholds.name: Exception ageing before escalation
thresholds.use: Escalate to the Head of Procurement

thresholds.name: Slow-moving lookback
thresholds.use: Zero issues in the lookback with stock on hand = slow-moving

thresholds.name: Requirement-proposal cover target
thresholds.use: Basis of the indicative purchase quantity (BRD FR-40)

thresholds.name: Stock-out tolerance
thresholds.use: Any critical item below 15 days of cover is a service risk

thresholds.name: Budget utilisation expectation
thresholds.use: Under or over this band requires explanation

model.name: Demand growth (annual)
model.basis: Programme growth trend over the reporting window
model.governs: Consumption value, purchase requirement, funding gap, cost per beneficiary

model.name: Service volume (beneficiary) growth
model.basis: Beneficiary trend in the service-delivery data

model.name: Project activity factor (next 12 months)
model.basis: Share of the next 12 months in which at least one project is active (from project end dates)

model.name: Price inflation (annual)
model.basis: Weighted average unit-price movement in the purchase history
model.governs: Consumption value, purchase value, funding gap, price variance

model.name: One-off price shock
model.basis: Scenario lever for a market, currency or contract event
model.governs: Consumption value, purchase value, funding gap

model.name: Supplier lead-time multiplier
model.basis: 1.00 = current average lead time of the supplier base
model.governs: Stock-out risk, safety stock, target stock, purchase requirement

model.name: Supplier on-time reliability
model.basis: Share of orders received within the agreed lead time

model.name: Target stock cover
model.basis: Policy: cover to hold after each purchase cycle
model.governs: Target stock level, purchase requirement, working capital, expiry risk

model.name: Safety stock
model.basis: Buffer against lead-time and demand variability

model.name: Maximum acceptable cover
model.basis: Above this, stock counts as overstocked

model.name: Expiry alert window
model.basis: Alert before expiry for redistribution or consumption

model.name: Wastage / write-off rate
model.basis: Observed expired and damaged stock as a share of consumption

model.name: Overstock redistributed
model.basis: Share of excess stock moved to a project with demand instead of being written off

model.name: Funding reduction
model.basis: Scenario lever for a grant reduction or donor hold
model.governs: Budget available, funding gap, budget utilisation

model.name: Budget growth / reallocation
model.basis: Approved additional budget or internal reallocation
model.governs: Budget available, funding gap, budget utilisation

model.name: Excess stock used instead of buying
model.basis: Share of stock held above the target cover that offsets new purchases (redistribution or planned drawdown)
model.governs: Purchase requirement, working capital, funding gap

model.name: Purchase cycle length
model.governs: Number of purchase cycles, order frequency, transaction load

scenarios.name: Baseline (current parameters)
scenarios.rationale: Reference case: current demand, price, supply and policy. Every other scenario is measured against this.

scenarios.name: Demand surge +20%
scenarios.rationale: Outbreak, flood response or a new campaign in the service area.

scenarios.name: Price shock +15%
scenarios.rationale: Currency depreciation, loss of a contract price or a supplier exit.

scenarios.name: Supply disruption (lead time x1.6, reliability 70%)
scenarios.rationale: Import delay, port congestion or a single-source supplier failing.

scenarios.name: Funding cut -20%
scenarios.rationale: Donor reduction or a hold on a grant instalment.

scenarios.name: Optimised policy (cover 60, safety 10, redistribute 60%)
scenarios.rationale: Tighter cover policy plus redistribution instead of new buying.

scenarios.name: Framework contracting (-8% price, lead time x0.8)
scenarios.rationale: Consolidate the top items into a framework agreement.

scenarios.name: Combined downside (demand +15%, price +10%, lead time x1.4, funding -10%)
scenarios.rationale: The plausible worst case: surge demand plus inflation plus supply delay plus a funding hold.

scenarios.name: Optimised response to the downside (S7 + policy and framework levers)
scenarios.rationale: Shows how much of the downside can be absorbed by levers available to management.
